messages.content:
What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: Not Specified
Medical Record Number: Not Specified
Date of Admission: Not Specified
Date of Discharge: Not Specified

INTRODUCTION:
The patient is an 81-year-old woman who visited the department of internal medicine in our hospital with complaints of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, and an upper abdominal mass. She had a history of left breast cancer 11 years ago. The patient was diagnosed with peritoneal metastasis of recurrent breast cancer and was put on endocrine therapy using letrozole.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient's symptoms improved with endocrine therapy, and she showed recovery from pleural metastasis and pleural effusion. Tumor marker values fluctuated during the course of treatment, with no abnormal CEA values obtained, and CA15-3 and BCA225 values gradually declining from the time of recurrence and returning to normal levels 2 years later. NCC-ST-439 value gradually increased up to 49 U/ml 6 months later, with a gradual decline thereafter along with the other tumor markers. The patient was currently receiving treatment in the outpatient department and is still alive on the same medication.

DISCHARGE OUTCOME:
The patient is being discharged in stable condition with continued endocrine therapy.

FOLLOW-UP:
No relapse of malignancy has been detected after a period of 6 years.

ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
Not Specified
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Letrozole.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Continue endocrine therapy as prescribed. Follow up with your healthcare provider as recommended.

text:
The principal diagnosis is most likely **C78.6, Secondary malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum**.

The admission was for peritoneal metastasis of recurrent breast cancer, presenting with loss of appetite, abdominal distension, and an upper abdominal mass. The original left breast cancer was treated 11 years earlier, so it is coded as history rather than as active disease:

- **Principal:** C78.6, secondary malignant neoplasm of peritoneum (the reason for admission)
- **Additional:** Z85.3, personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
- **Additional:** C78.2, secondary malignant neoplasm of pleura, since pleural metastasis is documented, though the summary describes it as resolved

Under ICD-10-AM sequencing rules, a secondary neoplasm is coded first when the primary is no longer present or under treatment. If the coder instead treats the breast cancer as the active condition under treatment, the principal diagnosis would be C50.912 (malignant neoplasm of unspecified site of left female breast) with C78.6 as a secondary code. The discharge diagnosis section is withheld, so a coder would need to confirm the attending physician's wording and the facility's coding guidelines before finalising.
